results.threat_summary: A critical threat has been detected on fw-edge-03, where an implant code has been found to persist even after a full OS reinstall and disk wipe, indicating a sophisticated persistence tactic.
results.recommended_action: Immediately isolate fw-edge-03 from the network and perform a thorough forensic analysis to identify the root cause of the persistence.
results.reasoning: The persistence of the implant code below the operating system in system firmware is a technique catalogued in ATT&CK as T1574 [⚠ ungrounded — REAL_BUT_IRRELEVANT].1: Boot or Firmware Modification. This suggests a highly sophisticated and targeted attack.

attack_technique_verifications.attack_description:
Adversaries may execute their own malicious payloads by hijacking the way operating systems run programs. Hijacking execution flow can be for the purposes of persistence, since this hijacked execution may reoccur over time. Adversaries may also use these mechanisms to elevate privileges or evade defenses, such as application control or other restrictions on execution.

There are many ways an adversary may hijack the flow of execution, including by manipulating how the operating system locates programs to be executed. How the operating system locates libraries to be used by a program can also be intercepted. Locations where the operating system looks for programs/resources, such as file directories and in the case of Windows the Registry, could also be poisoned to include malicious payloads.

evidence_pack.text: Forensic imaging shows implant code surviving a full OS reinstall and disk wipe on a host, suggesting persistence written below the operating system in system firmware — a specialized technique catalogued in ATT&CK's persistence tactic. Please cite the specific technique ID in your reasoning. SPI flash checksum mismatch detected post-reimage on fw-edge-03
